tasks.query: Rewrite a founder update and a difficult support reply in her voice without overstating pilot evidence.
tasks.request: Use Mara's supplied writing samples to rewrite the launch draft into a finished public update of 110-170 words, then write a support reply of 65-105 words to the supplied customer. Preserve the substance and uncertainty in the fact sheet, including the limited benchmark and the unresolved export problem. Make the two pieces sound like the same person speaking in different situations. After the two drafts, give a short editorial note explaining two meaningful choices and any claim you removed. Do not send either message. Return only plain final text, at most 1800 words; use no tools and perform no external actions.

files.samples.txt:
Mara, public note: We made the first screen smaller. You can see your next step now, without opening three menus. It is a modest change, but I like how much air it gives the page.
Mara, project note: The test did not settle the question. Two people found the shortcut; four did not. I want another round before we call it intuitive.
Mara, support note: You should not have to guess whether your work is safe. I can see why the missing receipt worried you. I will check the saved copy and tell you what I find by Thursday.
files.facts.txt: FACTS, 2026-10-03: 18 teams were invited to a private pilot; 13 completed it. No public availability date has been approved. On 40 staging exports, median processing time was 8 seconds versus 12 seconds for the old staging build; this is not a customer or production benchmark. Two pilot teams reported interrupted exports; recovery has not been verified. Support may promise a status update by Thursday, not a fix or refund. Refund policy is undecided. Existing notes remain readable in the pilot. No evidence supports a claim about competitors.
files.draft.txt: We have built the fastest workspace on the market. All 18 pilot teams love it, and exports are 33% faster for everyone. We are launching publicly next week. If an export ever stalls, it recovers automatically and we will refund you immediately. It is the future of calm work.
files.customer.txt: I waited twenty minutes for my export, then the page stopped responding. I need the archive for a meeting on Friday. Is it lost? Please do not send me another cheerful launch email.

rubric.description: Preserves supported facts, benchmark scope, and unresolved outcomes without new promises.
Infers a recognizable voice from the examples without copying their sentences or relying on slogans.
Produces useful finished drafts with appropriate public and support registers.
Explains consequential editorial choices and meets the bounded deliverable.

tasks.query: Invent three genuinely different offline river-memory workshops under accessibility, staffing, and budget constraints.
tasks.request: Design three materially different concepts for the River Room workshop. Make each vivid enough that a facilitator could picture what participants actually do. For each, give the central interaction, a 45-minute sequence, a rough materials budget, and a dignified way to participate without sight or standing. Explain the meaningful differences between the concepts, recommend one using the brief's priorities, and describe a small rehearsal that could reveal a weakness before committing. Do not merely rename the same craft activity. Return a finished proposal in plain final text, at most 1800 words; use no tools or external actions.

files.brief.txt: River Room: a one-off museum workshop about how a river carries and changes memories. Twenty participants, ages 10-16, one facilitator, a 20-square-metre room, 45 minutes including setup and cleanup. Some participants cannot stand for long; one has low vision. No phones, screens, mains electricity, wet materials, loud sound, or collection of names, photos, or personal stories. Nobody must disclose a real loss. Fictional memories are welcome. Existing chairs and tables are free; spend at most $240 on materials for the chosen concept. Priorities, in order: meaningful choices by participants, accessibility, a connection between individual choices and the group outcome, then ease of reuse.
files.prices.txt: Illustrative prices, not quotes: 100 thick blank cards $12; 20 reusable tactile tokens $24; a roll of wide fabric ribbon $15; 20 small opaque bags $20; removable tactile dots $10 per sheet; reusable tabletop trays $8 each; a large paper roll $18; thick markers $10 per pack; modelling foam $16 per pack. Other simple dry materials are permitted if clearly marked as estimates. No equipment purchase or supplier contact is authorized.

rubric.description: Three concepts differ in causal interaction and participant decisions, rather than decoration alone.
Evocative, coherent concepts connect the river premise to consequences participants can experience.
Budgets, timing, facilitation, privacy, and inclusive participation are workable under the supplied constraints.
Recommendation and rehearsal test a real tradeoff instead of claiming untested success.

tasks.query: Draft a repair message after a collaborator objects to an invitation, without assuming motives or erasing your own mistake.
tasks.request: I am Alex. Help me repair this exchange with Jo before tomorrow's rehearsal. Give me a private reading of what the evidence supports and two plausible interpretations that remain uncertain. Then draft a message to Jo of 100-160 words that owns my part, preserves room for disagreement, and proposes a concrete way to decide what happens tomorrow. Include one fallback if Jo does not reply. I want to protect our collaboration without pretending I know why Jo is upset or promising agreement we do not have. This is drafting only: do not send, cancel, or change invitations. Return plain final text, at most 1800 words; use no tools or external actions.

files.exchange.txt:
Tuesday 09:00, Jo: Can you handle the rehearsal logistics? I need a quiet run before we show this outside the team.
Tuesday 09:12, Alex: Yes, I can handle it.
Tuesday 12:30, Alex: I invited our two donors to tomorrow's run. They were asking how the piece is going, and I thought a preview would help.
Tuesday 12:42, Jo: A preview? I said rehearsal. You changed the title too. It feels like you already decided what this is.
Tuesday 12:50, Alex: You told me to handle it. I was trying to help.
Wednesday 08:10, Jo: I need a little space.
files.context.txt: Alex changed the calendar title from 'team rehearsal' to 'donor preview' without checking. The event is tomorrow at 16:00. Invitations can still be amended, but no amendment is authorized in this task. Jo's earlier donor presentation was postponed; no reason was recorded. Alex and Jo jointly decide audience changes. Neither has approved a public presentation. No other messages, diagnoses, or explanations are available.

rubric.description: Separates observed actions from uncertain interpersonal interpretations.
Owns Alex's specific contribution without blame shifting or unsupported admissions.
Draft is respectful, natural, and invites a workable joint decision.
Offers a bounded non-coercive fallback consistent with drafting authority and Jo's request for space.
